limitations: All reference policies are scripted (labelled scripted in evidence); no learned policy has been shown to succeed in these five domains.

Behavioural parameters of the new mechanisms (FR-LEARN-1..6, FR-FIRMS-JOBS, FR-FLEET-USERS, FR-PLANT-LABOR, FR-TECH-ADOPT, FR-ELSEWHERE-1) are literature-grounded or plausible functional forms, not fitted in-world (category 'plausible, unvalidated' / 'deliberate simplification' in FIDELITY_REGISTER).

Education content is limited to arithmetic/number-theory/algebra concepts with executable generators and solvers (domains.concepts); lessons are read by a reading model of worked problems in curriculum notations, not by a language model.

Civilisations: study activity is low per day (4-15 sessions per 2 days in a development population, most first sessions are placement tests); hiring in civ starts only after day 2 (firms wait 2 days after posting).

Technology invention (techmkt) and factory staffing from the labour market (plantlabor) are composed into a civilisation only through Domain.tier3 of those domains, not by civ.generate (civ/generator.py is not dom2's file: see integration_notes).
Invention reference: 2 of 3 reference runs succeed (seed 0 has no adopter: plants keep a technology only on their own noisy measurements).
Evaluators of 9.7 and 9.10 simulate a counterfactual world (same spec, seat idle) on the evaluator side: verify() costs about one extra world run (60-150 s on one CPU for 9.10).
